## Historical audit: S0291

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/test/bw_0005/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below are JSONL lines in this file. The supplied record contains no image pixels for independent inspection.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1, `model_request` | The task was to reconstruct an indoor scene and match camera, framing, objects and materials from one RGB image. The student interpreted a small inset as a classroom; that interpretation is not independently verified. |
| Initial build — lines 3–4, H `model_response` and step 1 `execute` | The program created multiple named assets: walls, windows, door, five shelves, tables, stools, rug and small objects. Colored primitives and floor-joint geometry suggest material families, but no image textures are used. Shelf and furniture components are grouped as child parts; grouping alone does not verify physical contact or reference accuracy. No human pose is modeled. |
| Review and revision — lines 9, 11, 13–14 | Step 1 built and rendered successfully, and its image was supplied back to H. H diagnosed an obstructing right wall, elevated camera, washed-out appearance, and small cabinets and rug. The executed revision shortened the wall, lowered the camera, changed lighting/colors, added shelf backs and chair backs, and retained surrounding furniture. These diagnoses are H’s observations, not independent visual verification. |
| Further exploration — lines 19, 21, 23–24 | After the successful second render was supplied to H, H described a distant, isolated-looking room, pale surfaces and short-looking windows. The third executed program moved the camera closer with a wider lens, lengthened windows, adjusted lighting and colors, and replaced chairs with stools while retaining the shelf/table layout. Whether these changes improved fidelity is unknown. |
| Result — lines 26, 28–30 | Step 3 build and render completed with return code 0; `execution_result` reported `ok: true` and a saved image, and step 3 was selected. This establishes technical execution, not geometric or visual correctness. No post-step-3 visual review or formal quality score appears. |

**Teacher input and autonomy.** No teacher message, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-driven execution appears in this student trajectory; adoption cannot be established. H independently revised after runner-supplied renders. The recorded H sessions show no tool calls and disabled external tools, although the runner separately executed the generated programs (lines 2, 12, 22).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** The observed outcome is a technically successful, nonempty third build with **unknown reconstruction correctness**, not evidence of formal visual success or algorithm failure. Camera, lighting, part contact, object coverage, material appearance and any scene pose cannot be independently checked without the images; H also marked the distant furnishings and contents uncertain. The transferable lesson is to distinguish executable renders and editable hierarchy from visual validation, and to test camera and local geometry hypotheses against actual views. The particular wall removal, window heights and stool substitutions are task-specific choices, not validated general rules.
